sentences.text: Since the petitioners in these petitions are challenging the very same proceedings, they are taken up together, heard and disposed of by a common order.

2. The petitioners are charge sheeted for the offence under Section 498A of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 alleging that, the marriage of the defacto complainant was solemnized with the accused No.1 on 15.5.2019.
At the time of marriage, the parents of the defacto complainant, as per the demands of the accused, have given dowry to the accused in the form of gold and cash.

3. It was further alleged that the petitioners-accused subjected the defacto complainant to cruelty both mentally and physically, and on 7.5.2020, the defacto complainant was thrown out of the matrimonial home, stating that she should not come back to the matrimonial home till she brings a sum of Rs.20 lakh from the parental home, and the petitioners- accused refused to take back the defacto complainant to the matrimonial home, stating that she will be allowed to enter the matrimonial home, only when she brings Rs.20 lakh from the parental home.
The cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate of the aforesaid offence is impugned in these petitions.

4. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioners submits that, on 14.2.2021, the accused lodged a complaint with the jurisdictional police, stating that there was a misunderstanding between the accused No.1 and his wife, and without any reason, the defacto complainant is threatening that, she would commit suicide, and accordingly the accused No.1 left the defacto complainant in the parental home, and requested the police to call the defacto complainant and advise her suitably.

She further submits that the FIR was lodged as an after thought, only after the accused No.1 sent a notice dated 28.6.2021 calling upon the defacto complainant to give consent for dissolving their marriage mutually.

Hence, she submits that the dispute between the parties arises out of marital discord,
however, given a criminal texture.

She further submits that except omnibus and general allegations,
there are no specific allegations as against each of the petitioners - accused, as to how, and in what manner, the accused subjected the defacto complainant to cruelty and also the demand to bring money from the parental home.

5. On the other hand, the learned counsel appearing for the 2nd respondent submits that there are specific allegations as against each of the accused, as to how, and in what manner, the accused subjected the defacto complainant to cruelty, and also the demand was made to bring money from the parental home.

The charge sheet material clearly discloses the commission of cognizable offence,
and the veracity of the allegation can be considered only after full fledged trial.

Hence, the Balachandar T N vs The State Of Karnataka on 14 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60643879/
4 cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate does not warrant any interference and sought for dismissal of the petition.

sentences.text: 6. I have examined the submissions of the learned counsel appearing for the parties.

7. It is undisputed that the defacto complainant in the FIR, alleged that she was thrown out of the matrimonial home on 7.5.2020, and on 14.2.2021, she along with her parents, brother and sister came to the matrimonial home and requested the petitioners - accused to take her back to the matrimonial home.

In the meanwhile, the accused No.1 had filed a complaint with the jurisdictional police station that the defacto complainant has threatened that she would commit suicide, and requested the police to call the defacto complainant and advise her suitably.
Thereafter, the notice was issued on 28.6.2021 by the accused No.1 calling upon the defacto complainant to give consent for dissolving the marriage mutually.
The said notice was refused by the defacto complainant, which is evident from the acknowledgement produced along with the petition at Annexure-E.
The defacto complainant without offering any explanation for the delay of nearly more than one year lodged the FIR.
The Apex Court in the case of State of A.P. v. M. Madhusudhan Rao reported in (2008) 15 SCC 582 has held

entities.text: State of A.P. v. M. Madhusudhan Rao reported in (2008) 15 SCC 582
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: as follows:
"30. Time and again, the object and importance of prompt lodging of the first information report has been highlighted.
Delay in lodging the first information report, more often than not, results in embellishment and exaggeration, which is a creature of an afterthought.

A delayed report not only gets bereft of the advantage of spontaneity, the danger of the introduction of a coloured version, an exaggerated account of the incident or a concocted story as a result of deliberations and consultations, also creeps in, casting a serious doubt on its veracity.

Therefore, it is essential that the delay in lodging the report should be satisfactorily explained."
8.

A perusal of the FIR, and the complaint lodged by the accused No.1 against the defacto complainant, and also the notice issued calling upon the defacto complainant to give consent for dissolving the marriage mutually, clearly implies that the dispute between the parties arises out of the marital discord, however, given a criminal texture.
In my view, the continuation of criminal proceedings will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) Criminal petitions stand disposed of.
ii) The impugned FIR dated 31.7.2021 in Crime No.120/2021 registered by the Basavanagudi Women's Police Station in Crl.P No.246/2022 is hereby quashed.
iii) The impugned proceedings in CC No.1532/2022 pending on the file of the 37th Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru, in Crl.P No.404/2022 is hereby quashed.
